title: EXTRACTORS key mismatch breaks incremental extraction
description: EXTRACTORS constant uses plural keys (:models, :controllers) but re_extract_unit looks up by singular type (:model, :controller). Incremental extraction silently fails to find the correct extractor for any unit.

title: Missing types in re_extract_unit
description: The case statement in re_extract_unit only handles :model, :controller, :service, :component. Missing: :job, :mailer, :graphql_type, :graphql_mutation, :graphql_resolver, :graphql_query, :rails_source.

title: API controllers silently omitted from extraction
description: Controller discovery uses ApplicationController.descendants, which misses controllers inheriting from ActionController::API. API-only controllers are invisible to extraction.

title: Config extractors default missing 4 of 8 types
description: Default extractors config only lists :models, :controllers, :services, :components. Missing: :jobs, :mailers, :graphql, :rails_source.

title: Missing app/graphql/ in incremental file patterns
description: Incremental rake task scans app/models/, app/controllers/, app/services/, app/components/ but not app/graphql/. GraphQL type changes are never detected.

title: Missing eager_load! in incremental path
description: Full extraction calls eager_load! but incremental path may skip it, meaning newly-added classes won't be found.

title: Token estimation underestimates Ruby code by 15-25%
description: The (length / 4.0).ceil heuristic underestimates tokens for Ruby code. Ruby syntax (symbols, do/end, underscored_names) produces more tokens per character than natural language.

title: ViewComponent metadata uses Phlex-specific patterns
description: Phlex extractor metadata structure is Phlex-specific. A future ViewComponent extractor needs different metadata patterns.

title: Score fusion in hybrid search is ad-hoc, needs RRF
description: merge_candidates uses ad-hoc weighted score fusion. Should use Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF): score(d) = sum(1/(k + rank_i(d))) where k=60.

title: SQL injection pattern in Pgvector adapter pseudocode
description: Pgvector build_where interpolates filter values directly into SQL. Should use parameterized queries.

title: No cross-encoder reranking stage in retrieval pipeline
description: Pipeline goes from initial ranking to context assembly with no reranking. Cross-encoder reranking would improve precision for code search.

title: Missing chunking for scopes and per-concern source
description: Scopes and per-concern chunks are specified in chunking strategy but not yet implemented in extraction.

title: Embedding pipeline has no resumability
description: No checkpoint mechanism for embedding pipeline. Mid-batch failures require starting over.

title: No agent-as-operator design (extraction management, pipeline diagnostics)
description: No design for agents running extraction, managing the embedding pipeline, or diagnosing failures. Agents can only consume, not operate.

title: No multi-agent coordination design
description: No design for multiple agents working with the same index concurrently. Missing: shared state model, locking, handoff patterns, token budget coordination.

title: No agent self-service and diagnostics design
description: No design for agents assessing retrieval quality, reporting gaps, or requesting improvements.

title: Concurrent indexing safety not documented
description: No documentation of which operations are safe for concurrent access and which require serialization.

title: Transitive invalidation not bridged between extraction and embedding
description: When extraction produces new units, the embedding layer needs notification. No design for this bridge.

title: Agent-driven operations not documented
description: No design for how agents trigger and monitor pipeline tasks (extraction, embedding, validation).

title: Fix token estimation inconsistency across docs

title: Wire console_eval behind WOODS_CONSOLE_UNSAFE_EVAL + EvalGuard (v0.2)
description: Embedded-mode console_eval is hard-refused at dispatch (EmbeddedExecutor#refusal_for), so EvalGuard is unreachable on the shipped path. The refusal message already advertises WOODS_CONSOLE_UNSAFE_EVAL + a Rails.env.production? rejection as the opt-in contract, but the execution wiring is not implemented. Deliver the full contract before running any Ruby: (1) gate on both config.console_unsafe_eval_enabled AND ENV['WOODS_CONSOLE_UNSAFE_EVAL']; (2) refuse unconditionally when Rails.env.production?; (3) run EvalGuard.check! before dispatch; (4) require Confirmation approval; (5) record the run in AuditLogger. Partial wiring is worse than the current refusal — ship all five or none. Tracked in issue #87 (option 2 deferral). RESOLVED: EmbeddedExecutor#handle_eval now runs all five controls (guard → confirmation → SafeContext → Timeout → audit). Server.build_embedded fails closed at boot when the flag is on but a Confirmation or audit-log path is missing.

title: Extract BridgeProtocol constants module from StubBridge
description: Issue #82 renamed Woods::Console::Bridge to StubBridge so the scaffold status is obvious. The downstream smell — flagged by both reviewers — is that the canonical protocol contract (SUPPORTED_TOOLS, TIER1_TOOLS, TOOL_HANDLERS) still lives on the stub class. EmbeddedExecutor::TIER1_TOOLS = StubBridge::TIER1_TOOLS reads as 'the real executor borrows constants from the stub', which is backwards. Extract a Woods::Console::BridgeProtocol module owning the three constants; have StubBridge include or reference it; update EmbeddedExecutor to read from BridgeProtocol directly. When the real bridge-process implementation lands it can claim the Bridge class name without the protocol contract migrating with it. Pre-existing doc-rot in docs/design/CONSOLE_SERVER.md (sections 107/118/130 still describe rails runner lib/woods/console/bridge.rb as if it works) is in scope for the same PR. RESOLVED: new lib/woods/console/bridge_protocol.rb owns SUPPORTED_TOOLS / TIER1_TOOLS / TOOL_HANDLERS. StubBridge references BridgeProtocol (top-level aliases keep StubBridge::SUPPORTED_TOOLS working for existing callers). EmbeddedExecutor reads TIER1_TOOLS = BridgeProtocol::TIER1_TOOLS and no longer imports bridge.rb. CONSOLE_SERVER.md Connection Modes section carries a callout that the three rails-runner configs describe the target bridge-process architecture, not the shipping state.

title: Wire extraction-side writes when the first durable GraphStore adapter lands
description: The boot-time hydration path (Bootstrapper.hydrated_graph_store) now raises Woods::Storage::InapplicableBackend when the configured graph_store reports durable? => true, mirroring the Snapshotter::Vector pattern for pgvector/Qdrant. This is a tripwire, not a solution: it loudly refuses to rebuild a durable store from dependency_graph.json at boot, but leaves the durable store empty because nothing populates it. When the first durable GraphStore adapter lands (:mysql, :pgvector_graph, Neo4j, etc.), that PR must also wire an extraction-side write path: graph edges are produced by Extractor, not Indexer, so the write hook belongs at the same seam that writes dependency_graph.json (see Extractor#extract_all around output_dir.join('dependency_graph.json')). The contract being honored is documented in lib/woods/storage/graph_store.rb Interface#durable? YARD, Bootstrapper.hydrated_graph_store YARD, and docs/design/PERSISTENCE_AND_BOOTSTRAP.md §3.5. Do NOT design a speculative write API before the concrete adapter exists — bulk-load semantics differ too much across backends (Postgres COPY vs MySQL batched INSERT vs Neo4j UNWIND+MERGE) and a speculative API will get rewritten.

title: Obsidian vault exporter (human graph-view + agent sidecar)
description: Export extraction artifacts to a self-contained Obsidian vault (folder of interlinked Markdown notes) so a human can explore the app in Obsidian's graph view + Bases, and an agent can load the whole topology from a _woods/ sidecar in one read. One note per unit; wikilinks encode dependencies; flat YAML frontmatter (nested props are unsupported by Obsidian Properties, so structured edges live in the sidecar + body). Reads the flat extraction output via IndexReader using raw_graph_data (string keys, persisted pagerank); all edges derive from a single in-memory edge_map (graph edges/reverse), per-unit JSON used only for note bodies. Bare-identifier keys throughout (the graph already merges cross-type id collisions upstream). Four passes: link map -> notes -> sidecar/MOC/.obsidian-config/Units.base -> guarded stale-sweep. Sweep and .obsidian writes are both gated behind a .woods-vault ownership sentinel + a 30% purge guard mirroring Unblocked. Zero new Configuration accessors (vault_path/include_source/include_framework/force_purge are constructor kwargs, exposed via WOODS_OBSIDIAN_* env in the rake task). include_framework covers rails_source only (gem_source is unreachable via IndexReader::TYPE_DIRS). Grounded in Steph Ango / kepano vault conventions + official Obsidian docs. Shipped in #143. RESOLVED: added lib/woods/atomic_file.rb + lib/woods/obsidian/{vault_exporter,note_builder,name_mapper,vault_assets,errors}.rb + the woods:obsidian/woods:vault rake task; 49 unit specs plus an end-to-end booted-app validation (spec/integration/booted_extraction_spec.rb) that exports a real spec/dummy extraction and asserts resolvable wikilinks, no dangling links, a bijective sidecar manifest, and byte-identical re-export; docs in docs/OBSIDIAN_INTEGRATION.md + README + CLAUDE.md.

title: Extract shared UnitFacts; migrate DocumentBuilder + NoteBuilder onto it
description: Woods::Obsidian::NoteBuilder (B-056) and Woods::Unblocked::DocumentBuilder independently walk unit metadata (associations-by-type, blast-radius buckets, entry points, side effects, schema highlights, deps/dependents-by-type). That selection/shaping logic is format-agnostic; only the final string assembly (plain-text + GitHub URIs vs wikilinks + frontmatter) diverges. Extract a Woods::Export::UnitFacts that turns a unit_data hash into a structured intermediate, and make both builders thin formatters over it, so a unit-type metadata change is fixed in one place. PREREQUISITE: Unblocked detects changes by hashing the rendered body (Exporter#fingerprint = SHA256(title + body)), and its specs guard determinism/structure but NOT byte-exact output, so a refactor could pass CI green yet force a one-time mass re-push. Before touching DocumentBuilder, add golden-output regression specs that pin its exact body bytes per unit type. Until this lands, B-056 mitigates drift with a shared metadata-shape fixture asserted by both spec suites. Tracked in #144. RESOLVED: added lib/woods/export/unit_facts.rb (associations_by_type, schema_highlights, blast_radius) + specs; added spec/unblocked/document_builder_golden_spec.rb pinning DocumentBuilder body bytes per unit type against spec/fixtures/unblocked/golden_units.rb + golden/*.md; migrated DocumentBuilder model_associations + model_schema_highlights onto UnitFacts with the golden suite confirming byte-identical output (no Unblocked re-push); migrated NoteBuilder associations onto UnitFacts and added a shared Schema section; GoldenUnits is now asserted by both the Unblocked golden suite and the Obsidian NoteBuilder suite as the shared metadata-shape fixture.

title: Qdrant adapter sends Woods identifiers as point IDs — every upsert 400s
description: Qdrant only accepts uint/UUID point IDs but the adapter passed Woods identifiers ("User", "User#chunk_0") straight through, so every upsert 400s and the Qdrant path was non-functional. Fixed: point ids are now UUIDv5 over a pinned namespace (Qdrant::POINT_ID_NAMESPACE), the identifier rides in the payload under `woods_identifier`, and search reverse-maps while delete translates through the same Qdrant.point_id so it can't compute a different id than the upsert did. Translation is confined to the adapter — pgvector and the in-memory store are untouched, and the Indexer needed no change. UUIDv5 is implemented in Woods::Util::UUID5 and unit-tested against the published DNS-namespace vectors for python.org and www.example.com. STILL UNVALIDATED AGAINST A LIVE QDRANT: that a real server accepts these upserts, that a re-embed of an unchanged unit replaces rather than duplicates, and that delete actually removes the point. All current coverage is against a mocked Net::HTTP. Tracked in GH #147.

title: Incremental embed against in-memory vector store discards vectors but advances checkpoint
description: index_incremental never persist_snapshots and process_units always advances checkpoint.json, so on :local/:shared_filesystem presets changed units embed into a throwaway store, nothing is written to dumps/, and the checkpoint skips them next run — unrecoverable without full re-embed. Fix: hydrate+persist in incremental mode, or do not advance checkpoint when unpersisted. Tracked in GH #148. RESOLVED: an incremental run now hydrates the in-memory vector store from dumps/latest and dumps again, the checkpoint is written only after the dump is promoted (interval saves suppressed on that path), and a checkpoint hit is honoured only when the dump actually holds a vector for that unit — so a checkpoint that ran ahead of its artifact self-heals into a re-embed instead of stranding the unit.

title: Notion Columns sync collapses same-named columns across models
description: Column pages are upserted by bare column name and found by title equality across the whole DB, so shared columns (id/created_at/updated_at) overwrite each other across models — the Columns DB collapses to one page per distinct name. Fix: qualify title (users.id) or filter lookup by Table relation. Tracked in GH #149.

title: Audit follow-ups: medium-severity correctness/robustness findings
description: HTTP transport concurrent-handler unsynchronized IndexReader cache + lazy pipeline mutex init; Notion/Unblocked POST retry on read-timeout duplicates; Retry-After to_f zeros HTTP-date form; CircuitBreaker half-open unlimited probes + reset on overlap; bootstrapper/reload string-keyed vector metadata vs symbol-keyed search filters. Tracked in GH #150. RESOLVED: the pipeline mutex initializes eagerly; IndexReader serializes shared cache bookkeeping; Woods::RetryAfter handles delta-seconds and HTTP-date values; CircuitBreaker admits one half-open probe and preserves overlapping failures; non-idempotent export POSTs do not retry ambiguous outcomes; and boot/reload vector metadata is normalized for indifferent filter matching.

title: Dependency graph collapses same-identifier units of different types onto one node
description: DependencyGraph keys nodes on the bare identifier, so two units of different types that share one (a Scenic view `reports` from db/views/reports_v01.sql and a factory `reports` from spec/factories/reports.rb) collapse onto a single node — last registration wins, and the loser also loses its type-index entry. Both unit JSON files are still written, so the index and the graph disagree. deduplicate_results only dedupes within a type. Surfaced by the #164 differential harness, which works around it by giving each generated artifact family its own name prefix. Fix likely means keying the graph on (type, identifier) or namespacing identifiers per type, which touches every graph consumer (MCP tools, Obsidian, retrieval). RESOLVED: #225 (PR #242) gave the graph typed node identity, and the release/2.0.0-readiness branch closed the remaining holes: wholesale replacement now prunes by (identifier, type), dependents serialize on every unit sharing an identifier, and incremental git enrichment keys on each type's own file path. B-100/#213 (type-prefixed identifiers for embed ids and export names) remains the open root-fix design.

title: Two files defining the same constant resolve differently in full vs incremental extraction
description: When two source files yielded units of the same type with the same identifier, full extraction kept the first by glob order while incremental extraction could retain a different writer. The source tree is already ambiguous in that state, and the index cannot represent both units. RESOLVED by G-1: per-type deduplication now records the retained source path and raises Woods::ExtractionError when a later unit derives the same type+identifier from a different file. Same-file re-derivation remains a legitimate deduplication case. Full extraction therefore fails closed instead of publishing a tie-break that can disagree with incremental extraction.

title: Phase 1-4 of the reactive index spike: in-process extractor API, woods:watch daemon, MCP freshness contract, multi-instance operation
description: Follow-on work from #164 now that phase 0 (incremental correctness + differential harness) has landed. Phase 1: a public API to re-run a single whole-app extractor against a booted app (WHOLE_APP_EXTRACTORS already does this internally). Phase 2: a resident file-watching daemon (woods:watch) — placement decision, restart triggers, storm handling, degraded status. Phase 3: a generation token IndexReader checks per request, plus working-tree staleness in woods_status. Phase 4: multi-worktree operation with per-daemon idle TTL. Each phase needs measurements against the success criteria in #164. RESOLVED: all four phases landed on claude/woods-issue-164-uu6tc0 (PR #165). Phase 1 = Extractor#refresh + woods:refresh + ReloadPolicy; phase 2 = Woods::Watch daemon + woods:watch; phase 3 = Woods::Generation + IndexReader self-refresh + woods_status freshness fields; phase 4 = PipelineLock write serialization, daemon deference for hook syncs, idle TTL, six-worktree spec. Outstanding and documented in docs/WATCH_DAEMON.md rather than tracked here: large-host-app latency, bind-mount event latency, and per-daemon memory at six-worktree scale — all three need a real host app.

title: Dependency graph persists absolute file paths, so the index is not portable off the machine that built it
description: dependency_graph.json stores absolute paths (file_map keys and nodes[].file_path) while every per-unit JSON stores relative ones. Ordering, not intent: extract_all rebuilds the graph at phase 1.6 and normalize_file_paths runs at phase 4.5, so registration captures the absolute string and the later reassignment of unit.file_path never reaches the copies in @nodes/@file_map. register_and_write has the same order, so full and incremental agree — this is not an equivalence bug and the #164 harness is right not to flag it. It matters for the documented Docker deployment (extraction inside the container, Index Server on the host reading the volume mount): the graph carries /app/... paths, so affected_by, identifiers_for_path and the prune sweep match nothing host-side, and a host-run woods:incremental computes an empty blast radius silently. A moved or renamed checkout has the same effect. Fix: normalize before registration and relativize at the lookup boundary. Needs a from_h migration for absolute-keyed graphs already on disk — same shape as normalize_edges and normalize_file_map, which handle pre-#164 formats without a rebuild. Surfaced by the #164 review (finding 17); deferred from PR #165 as too large for it. Tracked in GH #166.

title: GraphQL runtime introspection can emit units no per-file pass reproduces
description: GraphQLExtractor#extract_all runs a static file pass and a runtime pass (extract_from_runtime_type). PR #165 made the file pass unconditional, fixing the divergence visible without graphql-ruby loaded (the per-file path indexed types a full run dropped). Remaining: with the gem loaded, the runtime pass can emit units the file pass cannot reach — dynamically defined types, schema-builder/DSL types, anything whose constant exists only after the schema is constructed. Those units have no source file, so no changed path dispatches to them and an incremental run cannot recreate them. Fix is probably a discoverable_classes equivalent so the incremental path reconciles the runtime set in both directions like class-based types, provided the schema type map is exact by construction; otherwise move GraphQL to WHOLE_APP_EXTRACTORS. Either way needs gem 'graphql' in the version gemfiles as a dev/test dependency plus a harness template exercising a dynamic type — which is why it was left out of #165. Tracked in GH #167.

title: Framework units are permanently stale carry-over and woods-sync's Gemfile.lock advice cannot fix them
description: rails_source and gem_source units are written only by an explicit woods:extract_framework. Nothing automatic runs it — not bin/woods-sync, not the watch daemon, not woods:incremental, and not woods:extract — so once written they persist unchanged forever. Confirmed on a real host: 140 units (116 rails_source, 24 gem_source) carry host-style paths from a different worktree that resolve nowhere in either host or container; they were also the only units left absolute after #166, the same symptom. The sharp edge is that bin/woods-sync flags a Gemfile.lock change as 'only takes effect with a full extraction' and tells the user to clear .sync_head and re-run, but a full extraction is exactly what does not refresh framework units — so a Rails upgrade worktree keeps describing the old framework internals. The exclusion from incremental is deliberate and correct (WHOLE_APP_EXTRACTORS documents it); the gap is that 'changes only on dependency changes' was never wired to anything detecting one. Options in the issue; leaning toward refreshing on a lockfile-digest mismatch during full extraction plus a woods:validate warning. woods:validate has no unresolvable-file_path check at all, which would have surfaced this unprompted. NOTE: bin/woods-sync is NOT in this repo — it lives in the consuming application's repo, so the message fix and its full-only filter land there, not here. Preferred fix per review: make rails_source a Gemfile.lock-keyed WHOLE_APP_EXTRACTORS member rather than calling woods:extract_framework more often, since that task bypasses normalize_file_paths, the type index, the manifest, publish_generation AND the extraction lock. Tracked in GH #169.

title: woods:clean and the embed tasks write against the index unlocked
description: woods:clean is a bare FileUtils.rm_rf(output_dir) with no woods_with_extraction_lock. Run mid-cycle it removes the lock file itself, so the holder's release hits ENOENT (handled) and the next contender acquires immediately — two writers plus a daemon publishing into a deleted tree. Deliberate human action so frequency is low, but silent, and recovery is a full re-extraction. The fix is not simply 'take the lock', since the thing being deleted contains the lock: either delete everything except the lock file then release and remove it, or refuse to run while a daemon is alive the way woods:incremental stands down. woods:embed / woods:embed_incremental are also unlocked; arguably a separate concurrency domain since the daemon does not embed, but worth an explicit decision — PipelineGuard's cooldown reduces the window for full runs without serialising them, and incremental embeds are not rate-limited at all. Split out of #169, where the mechanism is unrelated and would have been closed alongside a fix that does not address it. Tracked in GH #170.

title: A no-op incremental embed no longer refreshes unit metadata, so a deleted unit stays retrievable
description: snapshot_worth_writing? gates persist_snapshot on stats[:processed], reasoning only about the vector store — sound for vectors (prune_superseded_vectors is reachable only from store_vectors) but persist_snapshot also writes metadata.msgpack, and persist_unit_metadata runs over load_units, which for index_incremental is every unit. So a zero-processed run rebuilds the metadata store and discards it. Delete a model, run woods:incremental then woods:embed_incremental: no source_hash changed so processed==0, and pre-fix metadata.msgpack was rewritten without the unit, making the stale vector inert (ContextAssembler#find_batch missed it). Post-fix both vector and metadata survive, so codebase_retrieve can return a deleted model as a live hit — stale vectors went from latent to visible. The gate does prevent a worse bug: a failed hydrate calls clear! and pre-fix would dump the emptied store over latest. Options: split the gate so only the vector dump is skipped; widen it to consider whether the unit set changed; or accept and document. Tracked in GH #171.

title: convention_path_unit? keys on unit type where the property is per-unit, so file-defined GraphQL units leave the deletion sweep
description: convention_path_unit? was widened to include GRAPHQL_TYPES so the prune sweep would stop deleting runtime-defined types in the same run that added them, but it keyed on unit type where the property is per-unit, so units the static file pass produced (real file behind them) were spared too and a deleted app/graphql/**.rb survived an unnamed-path sweep forever; the daemon catch-up, which runs an empty change set because deletions leave no mtime, was the exposed caller. RESOLVED at the source rather than in the predicate: source_file_for_class no longer fabricates an app/graphql/<constant>.rb fallback when nothing resolves, it returns nil, which is the honest answer and the only point where no-file-backs-this is knowable. DependencyGraph#register skips nil paths, so a runtime-defined unit never enters file_map and the path sweep cannot reach it; GraphQL then came back OUT of convention_path_unit? entirely, so file-defined types are swept like anything else. The two changes are a pair: removing GraphQL from the predicate is only safe because runtime-only units no longer carry a path. Two approaches were tried and rejected first, comparing the recorded path against the convention path derived from the constant (cannot discriminate, since Types::FooType conventionally lives AT its convention path) and letting the sweep prune then relying on the reconciler to re-add (exactly what except: pruned prevents). Reproduction is now a live harness example in incremental_equivalence_spec gap 2, mutation-verified against the predicate change. The #167-preservation half cannot be end-to-end tested without graphql-ruby, which is in no bundle; it rests on the source_file_for_class nil specs plus the register nil guard. Tracked in GH #171.

title: Railtie console-MCP wiring mounts BearerAuth/OriginGuard over the entire host app, and both enable flags are read before config/initializers run
description: railtie.rb:68 inserts OriginGuard and BearerAuth via app.middleware.use with no path scoping; BearerAuth 401s every request lacking the bearer header and OriginGuard 403s any non-loopback Host, so enabling the documented Rack console mode takes the whole host app down. Separately railtie.rb:13/:60 evaluate console_mcp_enabled/session_tracer_enabled at railtie-initializer time, which runs before :load_config_initializers, so setting either flag in config/initializers/woods.rb (the generator-created location every doc names) is a silent no-op. Fix: path-scope the guards (path: kwarg or compose inside Console::RackMiddleware after its path check) and decide enablement lazily at request time (or warn from after_initialize when the flag is set but nothing mounted). Verified against a booted railties 8.1 app. Acceptance: enabling via the initializer mounts and serves only the console path; GET / is untouched. Tracked in GH #183.

title: QueryClassifier target-type patterns match ordinary English words and hard-filter vector search with no fallback
description: TARGET_PATTERNS treat common words as type signals (\bget\b -> :route, \bemail\b -> :mailer, \bquery\b/\btype\b -> :graphql, \bperform\b -> :job) and SearchExecutor#build_vector_filters pushes classifier-derived target_type down as a HARD vector-metadata filter; unlike caller-supplied types there is no within-type fallback (retriever.rb:318 falls back only for caller type_list). 'How do we get the current user?' filters to route units only and can return an empty primary section. Fix: stop pushing classifier-derived target_type into the vector filter and let Ranker's soft type_match express it, or reuse within_type_fallback on empty results and tighten the worst patterns. Acceptance: the example queries return non-empty, sensible results on a non-route/non-graphql index. Tracked in GH #184.

title: Ranking layer is largely inert: matched_fields is dead code, raw RRF feeds 0-1 weights, ContextAssembler re-sorts by raw score, PageRank memo never invalidated on reload
description: Four compounding defects: (1) Ranker#keyword_score guards on candidate.matched_fields but SearchExecutor::Candidate has no such member anywhere in lib/, so 20% of the weight budget is permanently 0.0. (2) apply_rrf replaces scores with raw RRF values (max ~0.016/source) fed unnormalized into 0-1-scaled weighted scoring, so the 0.40 semantic weight contributes at most ~0.02 and metadata signals swamp fused relevance on every hybrid query. (3) ContextAssembler#assemble_section re-sorts by raw candidate.score, discarding the Ranker's weighted ordering entirely - recency/importance/type_match/diversity never influence what enters the context or what truncation cuts. (4) Ranker memoizes @pagerank_importance_map forever; Bootstrapper.reload_stores! swaps the graph in place but never invalidates it, so a long-lived woods-mcp-http serves boot-time percentiles after reload. Fix: populate matched_fields from the keyword path (or drop the signal and renormalize), min-max normalize RRF before weighting, make Ranker rewrite candidate.score to the weighted score (or preserve order in the assembler), and invalidate the memo from reload_stores!. Acceptance: a ranker-demoted candidate stays demoted in the assembled context; fused-relevance winner survives divergent recency/type metadata; reload picks up new PageRank. Tracked in GH #185.

title: ContextAssembler assembles the same framework unit into both :primary and :framework sections
description: Section membership is not disjoint: primary takes candidates.reject(:graph_expansion) which includes vector-sourced rails_source/gem_source units, and the framework section selects framework_candidate? over the same list - a framework unit retrieved by vector search is formatted twice in one context, spending both budgets on identical content (sources.uniq hides it from the attribution list). Fires precisely on framework_context queries whose top hits are rails_source units. Fix: exclude framework candidates from primary when the framework budget is active. Acceptance: each identifier's source text appears exactly once in the assembled context. Tracked in GH #186.

title: pgvector backend unusable via the documented path: ensure_schema! has no callers and the woods:pgvector generator creates dead schema
description: Pgvector reads/writes woods_vectors, created only by ensure_schema! - which nothing calls (Builder#build_vector_store instantiates the adapter bare). The documented setup (rails generate woods:pgvector && db:migrate) creates an embedding_vector column on woods_embeddings that has zero readers/writers in lib/. A user following every documented step gets PG::UndefinedTable on the first embed. Fix: call ensure_schema! from the builder (or lazily on first write) and rewrite/delete the generator so migrations manage the table actually used. Related: #181 (batch dedup). Acceptance: configure_with_preset(:postgresql) + woods:embed works against a fresh database. Tracked in GH #187.

title: RetryableProvider/CircuitBreaker are never wired - a single 429 aborts woods:embed and discards paid-for work
description: RetryableProvider and CircuitBreaker have zero production callers; Tasks.build_embed_indexer and Builder#build_retriever hand the raw provider to the pipeline, so any OpenAI 429/5xx raises Woods::Error and aborts the run. On :local/:shared_filesystem presets interval checkpoints are suppressed and the dump only lands at end-of-run, so a mid-run rate limit discards every embedding already paid for. Violates .claude/rules/storage-retrieval.md ('Never let a rate limit crash the indexing pipeline'). Fix: wrap providers in RetryableProvider + per-provider CircuitBreaker at both build sites; honor Retry-After on 429. Acceptance: a provider raising 429 twice then succeeding completes the run. Tracked in GH #188.

title: Bare File.read violations crash the embed pipeline, Unblocked sync, and StatusReporter under LANG=C
description: CLAUDE.md mandates AtomicFile.read for Woods' own JSON artifacts, but three satellites still use bare File.read + narrow rescues: Indexer#load_units (indexer.rb:91) crashes woods:embed with Encoding::InvalidByteSequenceError on any non-ASCII unit source under LANG=C (reproduced); load_checkpoint/save_checkpoint share the breach (save is also non-atomic); Unblocked SyncManifest#load (sync_manifest.rb:114) crashes every subsequent sync once a non-ASCII URI lands in the manifest, violating its own degrade-to-fresh contract (reproduced); StatusReporter reads manifest.json rescuing only JSON::ParserError. Fix: AtomicFile.read/.write everywhere, widen rescues to include EncodingError on degrade paths, add non-ASCII fixtures under forced US-ASCII external encoding. Consider a custom cop banning bare File.read/File.write under lib/woods. Tracked in GH #189.

title: Flow layer bypasses AtomicFile and persists absolute container paths into unit JSON and flow_index.json
description: FlowPrecomputer writes flow docs and flow_index.json with plain File.write (only index artifacts not using temp+fsync+rename) and stores ABSOLUTE paths in flow_map and unit metadata[:flow_paths], which Extractor#rewrite_flow_annotated_units persists into per-unit JSON - breaking the #166 portability contract (container /app/... paths served verbatim to host readers; identical trees at different roots produce different bytes). Read side (mcp/server.rb) uses bare File.read rescuing only JSON::ParserError/ENOENT, so an encoding error under LANG=C makes trace_flow return internal_error instead of degrading to query-time reassembly. Fix: relative paths (join against index_dir at read time, as load_precomputed_flow already does), AtomicFile both ways, rescue EncodingError into the reassembly fallback. Tracked in GH #190.

title: drop_vanished_units has no mass-deletion guard: an empty load_units wipes the vector index and rotates away good dumps
description: If an incremental embed run sees zero unit JSONs (mismatched WOODS_OUTPUT between shells, deleted extraction output, glob failure), every hydrated identifier counts as vanished: all vectors pruned, an effectively empty dump promoted, and three runs later retention (default 3) has evicted every dump that held real data (reproduced with the real Indexer). Obsidian/Unblocked gate destructive sweeps behind a 30% purge guard; this sweep has a post-hoc warn. Fix: refuse when current identifiers are empty but persisted ids are not; add a proportional guard (>30% vanished requires override), warning BEFORE deleting. Tracked in GH #191.

title: WVF1 idx ids hydrate as ASCII-8BIT so non-ASCII identifiers never match their UTF-8 twins - perpetual re-embed plus duplicate live entries
description: parse_idx builds ids with byteslice on a binread buffer, so hydrated ids are BINARY-tagged. A non-ASCII identifier is not eql? to the same bytes tagged UTF-8: @persisted_ids.key? misses (checkpoint self-heal re-embeds the unit every incremental run forever) and InMemory#store appends a second live entry instead of overwriting, doubling counts and search results per run. The existing spec asserts byte equality only, papering over it. Fix: force_encoding(UTF_8) in parse_idx (the format already documents UTF-8 bytes) and tighten the spec to include encoding. Tracked in GH #192.

title: Model concern inlining silently skipped for compact-style class definitions, and CallbackAnalyzer can never see concern-defined callbacks
description: build_model_source_with_concerns inserts the concern block via source.sub(/(class\s+<demodulized>.*$)/): compact-style 'class Library::Book < ApplicationRecord' never matches, so sub no-ops and the block is silently discarded while metadata.inlined_concerns still claims inlining happened; the missing \b also lets 'class BookmarkError' capture Book's insertion point. Separately, concern source is inlined as '# '-prefixed comments and that composite is handed to CallbackAnalyzer, whose Prism parse cannot see commented code - so the standard 'included do; before_save :set_slug; end' idiom always yields empty side_effects. Fix: match compact+nested forms with \b, append-with-warning fallback, derive inlined_concerns from actual insertion; give CallbackAnalyzer a parse-friendly composite (raw concern sources), keep comments for display only. Tracked in GH #193.

title: TestMappingExtractor mis-parses RSpec.describe Klass, type: :model (the rspec-rails generator default)
description: extract_rspec_subject's constant regex requires whitespace immediately after the constant, so the comma form never matches; the string fallback then matches the FIRST quoted describe anywhere in the file (typically an inner describe 'validations') and that string becomes subject_class and a :model dependency target - the real coverage edge is lost and ghost graph nodes are minted. Since ', type:' metadata is the generator default, most real host apps get a broken test->code mapping. Fix: allow [\s,] after the constant; anchor the string fallback to the file's first describe line; add specs for the metadata form. Tracked in GH #194.

title: Chunkers close methods at the first nested if/case/begin end; endless defs never close
description: All three chunkers track depth only for 'do' blocks (ModelChunker also def), never multi-line if/unless/case/begin/while - a guard-clause if...end mid-method terminates the chunk, misclassifying everything after it (plus the real closing end) into :summary with wrong chunk_type metadata. Endless defs (def show = ...) open a method that never closes, swallowing all subsequent methods (reproduced against the real chunker). Fix: reuse RakeTaskExtractor#block_opener?'s opener set, or better slice chunks by Ast::MethodExtractor (Prism) line ranges; skip method-tracking state for 'def x = expr'. Acceptance: the action chunk contains the method's final end and code following a nested if. Tracked in GH #195.

title: Standing-down daemon clobbers the live daemon's status file with 'stopped' and empties watch_pending.json
description: Daemon#run's ensure block runs on the early return :already_running path, so a correctly standing-down second daemon still executes persist_pending([]) and publish_status(:stopped) - overwriting the LIVE daemon's record under the stander-down's pid for up to HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL (300s). Every caller's stand-down logic inverts: a 'watch_status || start' hook immediately starts a third daemon (exactly the state the guard prevents), woods:incremental contends with the live lock, and carried-forward paths in watch_pending.json are lost (reproduced end-to-end). Fix: return before side-effecting state and guard the ensure (e.g. @started flag or inner run_started method). Acceptance: status record and watch_pending.json byte-identical after a stand-down. Tracked in GH #196.

title: PipelineLock#touch can resurrect a just-released lock as an ownerless phantom file
description: touch uses FileUtils.touch, which CREATES the file when missing. The heartbeat racing release (lock_ownership reads :ours, release renames+deletes, touch recreates) leaves a fresh 0-byte lock no process owns and no release will delete - every writer blocks for the full 600s stale window and manual rake runs exit 1 claiming a writer exists while none does (reproduced). Fix: refresh without create semantics - File.utime(t, t, path) (ENOENT already rescued by the method's SystemCallError rescue); optionally re-verify ownership on the same fd. Tracked in GH #197.

title: Failed extractor construction returns [] not nil (licensing prune of good units), and replace_type_wholesale removal ignores @eager_load_complete
description: Two twins of documented safety principles applied in one place but not the other. (1) extract_with_rule returns nil on per-file failure precisely so a transient failure cannot license pruning - but when the extractor INSTANCE fails to construct, extractor_for memoizes nil and 'return [] unless extractor.respond_to?' produces the 'path defines nothing' answer: a watcher batch then prunes every unit on those paths and bumps the generation. Fix: return nil when extractor_for yields nil. (2) stale_class_based_units gates removal on @eager_load_complete ('the whole safety argument'), but replace_type_wholesale performs the same discovery-set-driven removal ungated, and the routes cascade routes four descendants-discovered types through it - on a degraded (NameError-fallback) boot, one routes edit mass-deletes controller units. Fix: gate the removal loop for CLASS_BASED_DISCOVERY keys, warn when skipped. Tracked in GH #198.

title: Polymorphic associations emit phantom :model dependency edges
description: extract_dependencies maps every reflection to {type: :model, target: assoc.class_name, via: assoc.macro} without checking assoc.polymorphic?. belongs_to :commentable, polymorphic: true derives class_name 'Commentable' - an interface, not a model - producing an edge to a nonexistent node, or worse to the app's real Commentable CONCERN mislabeled as a :model/:belongs_to edge. Fix: emit via: :polymorphic_interface (or resolve concrete types from other models' as: options) instead of a :model edge. Tracked in GH #199.

title: ApplicationController and direct ActionController::Base subclasses are never indexed
description: discoverable_classes is ApplicationController.descendants (+ API descendants); Class#descendants excludes the receiver, so the app's richest controller (auth filters, rescue_froms, concern includes) is invisible in full-stack apps, and bespoke ActionController::Base subclasses never enter the index. The unguarded ApplicationController reference also raises NameError out of reconcile_class_based_types on hosts without the constant. Fix: discover from ActionController::Base.descendants + ActionController::API.descendants (defined?-guarded), filtered to app-defined classes by source path. Tracked in GH #200.

title: CachingExtractor assigns the file's first cache key/TTL to every cache_calls entry
description: extract_cache_calls iterates occurrences but calls extract_key_pattern/extract_ttl against the WHOLE source with String#match, which returns the first match in the file - every entry reports the first call's key_pattern and the first expires_in, wrong for any file with more than one cache call (the mainline case; reproduced with the extractor's verbatim regexes). Fix: iterate with MatchData positions and parse key/TTL from each call's own argument text. Spec: two calls produce two distinct key_patterns. Tracked in GH #201.

title: GraphQLExtractor#extract_class_name appends inner classes to the identifier, defeating runtime/file dedup
description: extract_class_name joins EVERY module/class declaration in the file, so a nested 'class InvalidInput < StandardError' inside a mutation yields Mutations::CreateUser::InvalidInput - the file-pass unit no longer collides with the runtime unit's correct identifier, so the class is indexed twice with the gem loaded, and without the gem only the wrong identifier exists and edges targeting the real name dangle. Fix: join only modules preceding the first class declaration plus that class name (same shape as the PORO/Lib half of the #174 family). Related: #174. Tracked in GH #202.

title: I18n and scheduled-job YAML with anchors/aliases is silently dropped (Psych 4 AliasesNotEnabled)
description: Neither YAML.safe_load call passes aliases: true; on Ruby 3.1+ any locale or schedule file using '<<: *defaults' (a widespread idiom) raises Psych::AliasesNotEnabled, converted by the surrounding rescue into a logged skip - the whole file vanishes from the index with no validate-level signal. Fix: aliases: true on both calls (alias expansion of already-permitted scalar types adds no deserialization risk); anchored-YAML specs. Tracked in GH #203.

title: Whenever block parser truncates at the substring 'end' inside class/command names
description: parse_whenever_blocks uses /every\s+(.+?)\s+do\s*\n(.*?)end/m - the terminator is neither word-bounded nor line-anchored, so the lazy body stops at the first literal 'end' anywhere, including inside CalendarSyncJob or WeekendDigest; the truncated body fails command detection, yielding command_type :unknown, no job_class, and no :job edge (reproduced with the real methods). Fix: line-anchor the terminator (^\s*end\s*$) or reuse RakeTaskExtractor's depth tracker; spec with a job name containing 'end'. Tracked in GH #204.

title: PageRank drops rank mass for duplicate edges and edges to unregistered targets
description: Out-degree counts raw edges but incoming contributions sum over the deduplicated @reverse Set - a source with both a :belongs_to and a :code_reference edge to one target (documented-normal) delivers half its mass; edges to unregistered targets leak entirely yet the node is not counted dangling. Reproduced: total mass decayed to 0.46 vs 1.0. Systematically under-ranks the most-referenced units, feeding retrieval ranking and exports. Fix: weight contributions by edge multiplicity; compute out-degree over resolvable edges and treat zero-resolvable nodes as dangling; extend the sum-to-one spec with duplicate-edge and unresolved-target cases. Tracked in GH #205.

title: SnapshotStore re-capture at the same git SHA orphans every previous unit-hash row
description: capture upserts with INSERT OR REPLACE keyed on UNIQUE(git_sha); REPLACE mints a NEW autoincrement id, the subsequent DELETE FROM woods_snapshot_units uses the new id and removes nothing, and PRAGMA foreign_keys is never enabled - so the ordinary edit-extract loop at an unchanged HEAD silently leaks a full unit set (~7k rows on a production-shaped host) per run, unboundedly (reproduced). Fix: INSERT ... ON CONFLICT(git_sha) DO UPDATE (keeps the rowid) or fetch-existing-id-first. Spec: double capture at one SHA leaves exactly units.size rows. Tracked in GH #206.

title: Notion exporter has no change detection - every sync re-upserts every page (2 API calls each at 3 rps)
description: Unlike Unblocked (manifest skips unchanged) and Obsidian (idempotent writes), Notion sync_all unconditionally upserts every model and column page, each costing a find_page_by_title query plus create/update through the 3 req/sec limiter - a 300-model app pays ~12,600 calls (~70 min) per run including no-op runs. Fix: persist a Notion sync manifest (page_id + content hash) under index_dir, skip unchanged pages, use cached page_id instead of the per-upsert title query. Related: #149 (fix keying first so the manifest keys are correct). Tracked in GH #207.

title: write_unit_file byte-compare skip is inert across runs: extracted_at defeats it
description: ExtractedUnit#to_h embeds extracted_at: Time.now.iso8601, so the serialized payload always differs from the previous run's file and identical_on_disk? never fires in its motivating scenario (wholesale replacement, ~1,707 units on a routes change) - the documented fsync-avoidance instead ADDS a read of every file and writes anyway. Fix: compare with the volatile key masked (mirroring VOLATILE_UNIT_KEYS in the equivalence oracle), or move extracted_at to the manifest; freeze time in the spec. Tracked in GH #208.

title: MetadataStore::SQLite#search interpolates field names into SQL unparameterized (latent)
description: search(query, fields:) builds json_extract(data, '$.#{'{'}field{'}'}') LIKE ? by string interpolation; a crafted field name breaks out of the JSON-path literal (injection confirmed mechanically). No production caller currently passes fields, so latent - but Interface documents fields as public, and pgvector's build_where shows the house standard (validate + quote). LIKE metacharacters (%/_) from the query are also unescaped in both adapters, silently broadening matches. Fix: validate field names against a whitelist regex and escape LIKE metacharacters. Tracked in GH #209.

title: Durable vector backends never prune stale vectors or metadata; checkpoint trusted blindly on store switch
description: Every staleness-removal mechanism is scoped to the in-memory/dump path — deleted units stay retrievable from pgvector/Qdrant even after a full woods:embed, and checkpoint_satisfied?'s hydrated-artifact check has no durable-backend equivalent (switching stores strands unchanged units unembedded). Extend vanished-unit reconciliation to durable deletes (Qdrant via .point_id) behind the #191 purge-guard thresholds; add a durable presence/identity check to the checkpoint. Tracked in GH #211. RESOLVED: added VectorStore::Interface#each_id (implemented by Pgvector via SELECT id, Qdrant via the paginated scroll API reverse-mapping point ids to Woods identifiers, and InMemory). Indexer#reconcile_durable_store deletes vectors for units the run never saw, on full and incremental runs alike, guarded by the same 30%/empty-load thresholds as #191. The same store read gives checkpoint_satisfied? a real presence check on durable backends, fixing the store-switch stranding. Proven against real pgvector and Qdrant in spec/integration/live_backends_spec.rb.

title: Evaluation harness has no working entry point — retrieval quality unmeasured
description: woods_evaluation.rake is never loaded and calls nonexistent accessors; nothing exercises the harness end-to-end, which is how the #185 ranking defects survived. Load it, fix the accessor surface against the hydrated retrieval path, add an offline smoke via the :fake provider, and run before/after ranking changes. Tracked in GH #212. RESOLVED: the railtie now loads woods_evaluation.rake alongside woods.rake; the rake bodies moved into a Woods::EvaluationTasks module (bare rake defs land on Object) and build the retriever through Woods::MCP::Bootstrapper so evaluation reads the same persisted index semantic search serves instead of fresh empty stores or four Woods.* accessors that never existed; MetadataStore gained all_identifiers (Interface + both adapters), without which every BaselineRunner strategy raised NoMethodError; spec/integration/evaluation_harness_spec.rb drives QuerySet -> Retriever -> Evaluator -> Metrics offline via the :fake provider, and spec/tasks/woods_rake_evaluate_spec.rb pins the baseline against the bootstrapper-hydrated metadata store.

title: B-062 root fix design: type-prefix identifiers for non-constant unit types
description: Prefix identifiers of non-constant unit types (factory:reports, database_view:reports, ...) so same-named units stop collapsing across the graph, embed ids, checkpoint, metadata, and export names. Requires an index migration (schema/generation bump + full re-extract/re-embed) and changes MCP-visible identifier forms — maintainer decision. PR #210 fixed the adapter-level symptoms; this is the root cause. Tracked in GH #213.

title: IndexValidator: no production caller and no dimension checking despite CLAUDE.md's claim
description: Nothing calls it and it contains no dimension-mismatch detection, so both halves of CLAUDE.md's 'IndexValidator detects this' are false. Wire a real provider-dimensions vs store-dimensions check into the embed/boot paths, or delete the class and fix the doc. Tracked in GH #214. RESOLVED: the false claim appeared in six documents (CLAUDE.md, AGENT_GUIDE, FAQ, TROUBLESHOOTING, RETRIEVAL_GUIDE, EMBEDDING_MODELS) plus the woods-diagnose skill; all corrected. IndexValidator is kept — it validates extraction-output integrity and is the oracle in multi_worktree_spec — with a class comment stating it knows nothing about vectors. The real check now exists: Pgvector#stored_dimensions (atttypmod) and Qdrant#stored_dimensions (collection config), compared against the provider by Tasks.verify_store_dimensions! before woods:embed builds an indexer, raising Woods::MCP::DimensionMismatch with the re-index remedy. Closes the durable-backend gap; the dump path already had this via Snapshotter::Vector.

title: Extractor polish: blockless factories, abstract-model phantom edges, private def visibility, Wisper false positives, manager capitalize
description: Five independent small defects from the review's low list; fix + regression spec each. See the issue checklist. Tracked in GH #215. RESOLVED: all five fixed with regression specs (blockless factories now parse without pushing an unmatched depth frame; ModelNameCache rejects abstract_class? models; extract_public_methods skips `private def`/`protected def` without disturbing section state; Wisper subscriber scanning is gated on the file mentioning Wisper at all, so socket.on(:message) no longer mints phantom events; manager wrapped-model derivation camelizes instead of capitalizing).

title: Flow/graph polish: resolve_target cost, case-branch operations, domain_clusters order, WVF1 header model name
description: Four small items from the review's low list; see the issue checklist. domain_clusters is the one analyzer output outside the determinism guarantee. Tracked in GH #216. RESOLVED: find_node_by_suffix is now backed by a memoized index on DependencyGraph (invalidated wherever @to_h is), replacing a per-operation linear scan and making a tied short name resolve deterministically; handle_case walks only the branches and reports the predicate as the condition; domain_clusters tie-breaks every max_by/min_by on identifier and sorts members/entry_points/boundary_edges, guarded by a new registration-order rotation spec (it sits outside analyze(), so the existing rotation guard could not see it); Indexer#persist_snapshot passes resolved_config so the WVF1 header records the model name.

title: Export-client hardening: Unblocked budget/redaction, unbounded Retry-After, DocumentBuilder URIs, Notion auth fast-abort
description: Five residual hardening items after the PR #210 idempotency/corruption/change-detection work; see the issue checklist. Tracked in GH #217. RESOLVED: the Unblocked budget is now honestly documented as a per-run cap (the real limit is server-side against a token shared across machines, so a persisted local counter would be wrong in both directions while looking authoritative); the Unblocked client redacts its bearer token on all three error paths, matching Notion; RetryAfter owns a 120s cap so every caller including both export clients gets it; DocumentBuilder cites the ref from the index manifest instead of a hardcoded main and percent-encodes path segments; Notion raises a typed AuthenticationError on 401/403 which the exporter re-raises instead of collecting per unit.

title: Retrieval/observability residuals: adapter search-semantics divergence, QuerySet taxonomy, IndexReader LRU note, GapDetector counting, RedisStore recency
description: Grouped low-severity residuals; the IndexReader item is the documented benign remainder of #150 item 1. See the issue checklist. Tracked in GH #218. PARTIAL (#218): ranker chunk-suffix, metadata search-semantics contract, IndexReader LRU synchronization, GapDetector query counting and RedisStore recency all fixed. The QuerySet intent/scope taxonomy item is handled with B-099/#212, which is where the harness that consumes it lives. QuerySet taxonomy also done: VALID_INTENTS/VALID_SCOPES now ARE QueryClassifier::INTENTS/SCOPES, with a legacy mapping accepted on load, so ground-truth annotations are comparable with pipeline output.

title: Test hygiene: unverified string-named instance_doubles, Phlex coverage, fixture-spec standalone require
description: String-named instance_doubles verify nothing (how #181's batch shape survived); PhlexExtractor is effectively untested; controller_extractor_fixture_spec fails standalone for want of require 'woods'. Tracked in GH #219.

title: CI gaps: no main-push runs, no Ruby 3.4/Rails 8.1 rows, no live-backend lane
description: pull_request-only trigger leaves merged main untested; the matrix omits Ruby 3.4 and Rails 8.1; every external protocol boundary is doubles-only — a services lane running the storage contract specs plus the offline embed->retrieve round trip closes the seam. Coordinate with woods-testbed#2. Tracked in GH #220.

title: persistable? treats durable vector stores as dumpable, crashing every pgvector/Qdrant embed run
description: Indexer#persistable? asked vector_store.respond_to?(:each_entry), but Storage::VectorStore::Interface *defines* each_entry (a NotImplementedError raise) and bulk_load, and every adapter includes it — so pgvector and Qdrant answered true. persist_snapshot then drove Snapshotter::Vector.dump into the raise at the end of an otherwise-successful run, discarding the whole embed pass. Fixed by asking which module owns the method (implements_own?) instead of respond_to?. Found by the new live-backend CI lane (B-107). Also fixed alongside: Qdrant mutating point operations did not pass wait=true, so acknowledged-but-unapplied writes read back stale — delete-then-count and write-then-dump both observed pre-mutation state.

title: Four extractor specs only pass in the company of the full suite
description: i18n (15/15), mailer (24/32), rails_source (33/33) and view_component (16/23) specs failed when run as a single file: the 'extractor setup' shared context referenced Woods::ModelNameCache without requiring it, and mailer/view_component called Woods.configuration without require 'woods' — so extraction raised, the rescue logged it, and every assertion hit a nil unit. All four passed in the full suite because earlier files loaded the constants first, which hides real breakage until someone bisects a single file. Found during the B-106 sweep (GH #219); verified pre-existing by stashing. A follow-up per-directory sweep found five more files in the same state — server_spec/snapshot_tools_spec (real-constant instance_doubles from the 98b9280 sweep), note_builder/vault_exporter/context_assembler (same) — all fixed by requiring the constants the doubles verify against. Same hermeticity class, different vector: git_provenance_spec's temp repos inherited the host's global commit.gpgsign, so a machine whose signer is unavailable (locked 1Password agent) hung or failed 3 examples; the repos now pin commit.gpgsign=false.

title: MCP pipeline_extract dies with NameError in a standalone woods-mcp process
description: The pipeline_extract tool's background run called Woods::Extractor.new directly, but exe/woods-mcp deliberately loads no extraction machinery and lib/woods.rb only lazy-requires the extractor inside Woods.extract!. In a standalone index-server process every pipeline_extract invocation therefore failed in the background with NameError: uninitialized constant Woods::Extractor — rescued and logged, so the tool reported 'started' and nothing landed. Invisible to the in-suite operator specs because other spec files load the constant first; surfaced by the B-109 per-directory standalone sweep. Fixed with the same lazy require Woods.extract! uses, pinned by a subprocess regression spec (spec/mcp/pipeline_extract_standalone_spec.rb) proven to fail against the reverted code.

title: Lift the mcp gem cap to 1.x and stop pinning the protocol version backwards
description: The gemspec pins `mcp >= 0.9.2, < 1.0`, which holds Woods at SDK 0.25.0 — two minor releases short of 1.2.0, the version that completed the MCP 2026-07-28 server lifecycle Woods depends on. Separately, exe/woods-mcp-start hard-defaults MCP_PROTOCOL_VERSION=2024-11-05, the oldest protocol in existence, and it is the documented .mcp.json entry point — so every user following the setup docs is opted out of version negotiation, server/discover and cache hints. Lift the pin to `>= 1.2, < 2.0`; delete the protocol default from the wrapper while keeping the env var as an escape hatch for stubborn legacy clients. The APIs Woods calls (MCP::Server.new, define_tool, Tool::Response, both transports, MCP::Configuration) are unchanged across 0.9.2..1.2.0 — every SDK breaking change (0.10.0 notify_progress/handler overrides, 0.15.0 MCP::Transports) predates the current floor. Ruby floor is unaffected: mcp 1.2.0 needs >= 2.7.0, Woods declares >= 3.0.0, and the rails-6.0 testbed variant on Ruby 3.0 stays supported — assert this with a CI row rather than trusting it. Gates B-112, B-113 and B-114. Acceptance: a legacy client and a modern client both work against one unmodified woods-mcp process (the SDK server is dual-era, and NOT pinning a version is what keeps it that way); server/discover returns Woods' capabilities; no Ruby or Rails floor moves. See docs/design/MCP_2026_STRATEGY.md. RESOLVED: gemspec now `mcp >= 1.2, < 2.0`; the MCP slice passed after updating modern HTTP requests to send the required Mcp-Method header and reading serverInfo from discovery _meta. exe/woods-mcp-start no longer defaults MCP_PROTOCOL_VERSION and announces on stderr when an operator pins one. Verified dual-era against a real built server in spec/mcp/modern_lifecycle_spec.rb: server/discover answers, a handshake-free tools/call succeeds, and a legacy `initialize` is still served by the same process. Ruby floor unmoved (mcp 1.2.0 needs >= 2.7.0).

title: Stateless Streamable HTTP — a woods-mcp-http restart should be invisible to clients
description: exe/woods-mcp-http builds StreamableHTTPTransport.new(server) with no `stateless:` flag, so it mints Mcp-Session-Id, tracks sessions server-side and serves the GET SSE endpoint. Restarting the server therefore invalidates every client session — a routine event (gem update, machine sleep, worktree rebuild) that currently forces every connected client through a re-initialize. MCP 2026-07-28 removes protocol-level sessions entirely (SEP-2567), so `stateless: true` makes restart invisible and makes the HTTP server horizontally deployable for the first time: any POST can land on any instance, which matters for the Docker split architecture and multi-worktree setups reading one volume-mounted index. Gate on WOODS_MCP_HTTP_STATELESS defaulting to ON, keeping session mode for one deprecation window — the one real break is users relying on Mcp-Session-Id, since GET stops serving the standalone SSE stream and the header disappears from the documented CORS contract. The spec also removes SSE resumability (Last-Event-ID); that is near-free for Woods because every index tool is a short JSON read, and the only long operations (pipeline_extract/pipeline_embed) are already fire-and-forget and move to Tasks under B-113. Depends on B-111. See docs/design/MCP_2026_STRATEGY.md. RESOLVED: exe/woods-mcp-http passes `stateless: true` unless WOODS_MCP_HTTP_STATELESS is 0/false/no, and the startup banner names the mode. docs/MCP_HTTP_TRANSPORT.md gains a Statelessness section with a behaviour table (GET -> 405, DELETE -> SDK no-op 200, no Mcp-Session-Id, no server-initiated notifications) and drops Mcp-Session-Id from the documented CORS contract for the default mode.

title: Adopt the Tasks extension for pipeline_extract/pipeline_embed, replacing the hand-rolled async protocol
description: pipeline_extract spawns Thread.new and returns {status: 'started'}; the agent never hears from it again and must poll pipeline_status to guess the outcome. If the MCP process dies mid-run the thread dies with it and no durable record survives. Around this sits a hand-rolled async job protocol: @pipeline_mutex, @pipeline_in_flight, pipeline_start/pipeline_finish, PIPELINE_LOCK_WAIT, acquire_lock_briefly, plus pipeline_status/diagnose/repair. The io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks extension standardises exactly this — advertise it, and when a client declares support return a CreateTaskResult with a durable taskId, ttlMs and pollIntervalMs, serving tasks/get, tasks/update and tasks/cancel. When the client does NOT declare support, fall back to today's behaviour verbatim: the spec forbids returning a task to a client that did not opt in, and that fallback IS the old-client compatibility story. Buys a real completion signal (success/failure with the error, not a poll-and-guess), disconnect survival (a task ID is durable — client restarts and resumes polling), cooperative cancellation against a LockHeartbeat-guarded run (inexpressible today), and deletion of the bespoke machinery, narrowing pipeline_status to reporting index state rather than doubling as a job-status endpoint. The durable task store must outlive the process to deliver the crash-resilience claim; the natural substrate is the index directory Woods already writes atomically — and any new writer against it MUST take PipelineLock (unlocked writers are how #169/#170 happened). Depends on B-111. See docs/design/MCP_2026_STRATEGY.md. RESOLVED: the mcp gem does not implement the Tasks extension (no tasks/* methods), so Woods supplies the extension methods, durable store, and tool-handler opt-in bridge. New lib/woods/mcp/tasks/: Store (durable one-file-per-task registry under <index_dir>/tasks/, AtomicFile writes, terminal-state guard, ttl sweep, and orphan detection that resolves a `working` record whose owning pid is gone to `failed`), Extension (capability advertisement + tasks/get, tasks/cancel, tasks/update via define_custom_method), and RequestCapture (a call_tool prepend that reads the request _meta envelope and exposes the opt-in to tool handlers via a thread-local, cleared in an ensure because Puma reuses request threads). pipeline_extract and pipeline_embed now share run_pipeline_in_background, which returns a CreateTaskResult to an opted-in client and the previous {status: 'started'} to everyone else, and records completion OR failure on the task. NOT done as originally scoped: @pipeline_in_flight / pipeline_start / pipeline_finish are kept. The task registry replaces the status-reporting half but the in-process mutex still has a job (cheap same-process exclusion without a disk read per call), so removing it would trade correctness-neutral code for a slower guard. The store deliberately does NOT take PipelineLock: records are one-file-per-task with no cross-file consistency to protect, and taking it would deadlock, since pipeline_extract holds that lock for exactly the span its task record needs updating. Task creation failure (read-only index dir) degrades to fire-and-forget rather than failing the tool.

title: Generation-driven change notifications (blocked on SDK subscriptions/listen)
description: PARTIALLY RESOLVED. Done: (1) tools are sorted by name after all conditional registration, in both the index and console servers, via the shared Woods::MCP::ProtocolPolicy — so a host with Notion wired advertises the same order as one without, which is what the spec asks for to keep an LLM's prompt cache warm, and which also fixes cursor pagination (the SDK paginates by offset over that previously-unordered collection). (2) SEP-2549 cache hints: cacheScope is pinned to 'private' and deliberately not configurable, because every result describes the user's own codebase and the SDK's fallback when only ttl_ms is set is 'public' — so setting a ttl and leaving the scope alone is exactly the combination that would let a shared proxy re-serve one user's source to another; ttlMs defaults to 10s (WOODS_MCP_CACHE_TTL_MS) chosen to be safe for the most volatile result the SDK applies it to, and a malformed override falls back rather than raising. BLOCKED: the generation-driven push. Two independent walls. (a) Stateless HTTP has no notification channel at all -- the SDK's send_notification opens with `return false if @stateless` -- so having made statelessness the default in B-112 there is nothing to push on. (b) subscriptions/listen is the 2026-07-28 opt-in mechanism and the SDK does not implement it, while the spec says a server MUST NOT send notification types the client has not explicitly requested -- so there is no conforming way for a client to ask, and pushing anyway would violate that MUST. Implementing it would mean building a long-lived SSE response stream inside a transport built to hold none. Cost of waiting is bounded: IndexReader#ensure_fresh! is the correctness path and is untouched, so an agent never reads a stale index -- it just learns of a change on its next call rather than immediately, exactly the relationship the reload tool already has. Revisit when the SDK ships subscriptions/listen.

title: Per-request modern envelope validation is handled by mcp 1.2.0
description: RESOLVED UPSTREAM: MCP 2026-07-28 requires a server to reject a request whose protocolVersion it does not support with UnsupportedProtocolVersionError (-32022) and a supported list. mcp 1.2.0 now invokes RequestEnvelope.parse! on the server path, so Woods no longer needs a local prepend. Acceptance: a modern request with protocolVersion 1900-01-01 returns -32022, while legacy initialize and supported modern requests keep working.

title: resultType emission is handled by mcp 1.2.0
description: RESOLVED UPSTREAM: MCP 2026-07-28 requires resultType on every modern result. mcp 1.2.0 stamps ordinary modern results with resultType complete, and Woods Tasks results keep their explicit task/complete result types. No local response-stamping prepend is needed.

title: Validate the MCP 2026-07-28 protocol work against a booted Rails host
description: None of B-111/112/113/114 has been exercised against a booted Rails app -- the authoring environment had the Docker binary but no daemon, so woods-testbed was unusable. Two things the unit suite cannot reach. (1) pipeline_extract against a REAL extraction: every task-lifecycle spec stubs Woods::Extractor, so nothing has watched a genuine multi-second run move a task working -> completed, nor confirmed the LockHeartbeat and task-completion interleaving under real timing. (2) The task store on a real index directory alongside a live watch daemon and genuine PipelineLock contention -- the argument that task records need no lock (one file per task, no cross-file consistency) is reasoned in the code and unit-tested but never observed under concurrency. Also worth confirming the store degrades correctly when the index dir is a read-only mount, which is a real Docker split-architecture setup. Put the smoke script in woods-testbed scripts/ so it runs unchanged against rails-6.0/7.2/8.0. See docs/design/MCP_2026_NEXT_STEPS.md 4.1.

title: Upstream remaining mcp gem extension gaps
description: mcp 1.2.0 now handles the core 2026-07-28 server lifecycle: RequestEnvelope validation, resultType, header mismatch errors, Mcp-Method/Mcp-Name validation, stateless HTTP and server/discover. The remaining gaps relevant to Woods are extension-level: no native Tasks extension and no subscriptions/listen. Woods compensates locally for Tasks with Tasks::Extension and a durable Store; subscriptions/listen still blocks generation-driven push notifications. Filing issues or PRs upstream would let Woods delete local protocol-extension code when native support lands.

title: Metadata-only unit changes never reach the promoted dump on local presets
description: snapshot_worth_writing? gates on processed/vanished counts, and the skip decision is source_hash (source only). A rename or dependency change with unchanged source leaves processed=0, so metadata.msgpack and per-vector file_path metadata keep the old path until an unrelated unit changes. B-069's shape for mutation instead of deletion; durable presets are unaffected (SQLite metadata store writes every run). Fix direction: compare non-source metadata against the hydrated dump, or fold file_path/deps into the checkpoint hash.

title: rubocop-rspec is installed but never loaded as a plugin
description: .rubocop.yml has no plugins:/require: entry for rubocop-rspec, so every RSpec cop is inert despite the gem being installed. Enabling repo-wide floods 300+ spec files with offenses, so it needs its own pass: enable, auto-gen a todo file, then burn it down.

title: Four spec files fail when run standalone
description: These pass in the full suite but fail standalone (missing requires / shared state): i18n 15/15, mailer 24/32, rails_source 33/33, view_component 16/23 at last measurement. A spec that only passes with company hides real breakage until someone bisects a single file. Same class as the controller_extractor_fixture_spec require fixed in #219.

title: woods:install migrations create three tables nothing reads or writes
description: The generator's migrations 001-003 create woods_units/woods_edges/woods_embeddings, but no runtime code reads or writes them: the SQLite metadata store uses its own units table and pgvector uses woods_vectors. Every install host gets three permanently empty tables plus migration ceremony. Either wire them to a real store or drop them from the generator (with an upgrade note).

title: config.extractors accepts a selection that nothing implements
description: The accessor validates and stores an extractor list, but extraction always runs all 34 (EXTRACTORS is frozen and never filtered by config). As of 2.0.0 setting a non-default value warns and the docs stopped teaching it as live. Decide for 2.1: implement selection (interacts with PathDispatcher, whole-app triggers, and incremental equivalence) or remove the accessor with a deprecation cycle.

title: woods.rake defines ~12 bare helper methods on Object in every host app
description: Top-level method definitions in a rake file land on Object in the host app. woods_evaluation.rake documents this exact hazard as the reason it module-wraps; woods.rake does not. The woods_ prefix makes collisions unlikely; module-wrap for consistency when convenient.

title: EXPLAIN (options) without ANALYZE is rejected by the function allowlist
description: check_function_allowlist! treats `EXPLAIN (` as a function call, so any parenthesized option list is refused even though the class docstring says EXPLAIN without ANALYZE is permitted. Found during the 2.0.0 readiness review; the ANALYZE/ANALYSE rejection itself is correct.

title: Rake task identifier is the bare task name, so a task reopened in two .rake files collides
description: A full run keeps the first-globbed file and warns; an incremental run on the second file overwrites the unit with the second file's path and source. Qualify the identifier with the defining file or merge sources per task.

title: Route identifier `VERB path` collides for routes that differ only by constraint
description: Subdomain, header-versioned, and format-constrained routes sharing a verb and path are deduplicated down to the first one, so the index is missing routes. Fold the constraint into the identifier.

title: Resilience::IndexValidator and woods:validate are two implementations of one check
description: IndexValidator is only used by spec/integration/multi_worktree_spec.rb as the stand-in for woods:validate, while the rake task has its own inline implementation. Make the task call the class, or delete the class and assert through the task.

title: First woods_status call blocks on a synchronous update-check probe
description: The update-check registry probe runs synchronously on the first woods_status call, adding a registry round trip (~1.5s worst case) to that response. Behavior is correct today, only slower; version semantics are already fixed by the merged update-check correctness work. Deferred from the v2.0 remediation plan (P7 / PR-7b): the async move is thread-lifecycle risk (probe on a bounded background thread, shutdown joins or abandons without hanging the exe, first call returns cached-or-unknown immediately, probe failure falls back to cached and self-heals on cache expiry) for a latency-only win. Rollback/current-correctness: current synchronous behavior is correct and stays the documented behavior until this lands; any future implementation reverts to it cleanly with no data, protocol, or format impact.

title: Runner-driven incremental extraction can read stale loaded constants
description: Driving extract_changed directly from a `rails runner` produced units whose source_code was current but whose loaded constants (and therefore metadata such as resolved actions) were stale, even when the boot postdated the edit: runner_command.rb wraps the script in Rails.application.executor.wrap, and prepare_incremental_run's safe_eager_load! behaves differently under it than under a rake boot. The documented CLI invocation (CHANGED_FILES + bin/rails woods:incremental) is correct; the gem's own flow_incremental_spec.rb works around the same hazard in-process by force-loading the edited file. Found while writing the testbed flows smoke. Disposition: document the CLI path as the supported incremental invocation, or make runner-driven incremental reload constants before extraction; investigation needed before choosing.

title: Factory units embed the full file source; an N-factory file is stored N times
description: Each factory unit's source_code embeds the entire factory file source (build_source_annotation), so a file defining N factories serializes that source N times in payloads. The audit flagged this as a storage item (v2-prerelease-audit P9b); PR-8 owned the item but deferred it because every available fix is a behavior or format change, and PR-8 was scoped to behavior-preserving refactors. The extractor already reads each file once and shares one String across the N units, so the remaining cost is on-disk duplication only. The decision needed: (a) slice per-factory source (parse_factories tracks open_depth; add end-line capture, scope source_code to the factory block) - changes unit source_code bytes, source_hash, search phase-2 matching, and forces a one-time re-embed of every factory unit; or (b) deduplicate identical source strings in the payload store (content-addressed segments) - an artifact-format change with reader compatibility and schema-version implications. Compatibility implications: option (a) changes generated artifact content and retrieval behavior (a query matching text in a sibling factory's block would no longer match that factory's unit); option (b) changes the payload layout and requires a version-gated reader path. Acceptance criteria: a chosen option documented here or in a superseding note; for (a), extracted-identifier AND source-hash before/after comparison attached for review plus one-time re-embed accounting; for (b), payload schema version bump, reader compatibility for old payloads, and round-trip validation; either way, factory_extractor specs updated to pin the new source_code contract and the audit's storage item closed.

title: recent_changes loads every unit file in scope per call
description: The recent_changes tool resolves git modification dates by loading unit files per index entry, O(total units) file reads per tool call against a 50-entry LRU, on indexes with thousands of units (v2-prerelease-audit P3). PR-8 deferred it: a correct fix needs an artifact-format design first, not a refactor. Candidate designs: digest-based short-circuit keyed off data already in the per-type index entries (skip loading units whose index-level digest is unchanged), or a payload-store bulk read that materializes git metadata in one pass. Compatibility implications: any new index-side field (e.g. a per-entry git digest) is an artifact-format addition that older readers must ignore and older indexes must tolerate; the tool response shape must stay identical.
